THE OBSERVATION

Look closely.

Compare Spanish decks of 40 or 48 cards, a standard 52-card American deck, and the 78-card Tarot de Marseille. Record the deck and spread before interpretation. The Marseille catalog keeps Justice at VIII and Strength at XI; the app uses schematic Kamala faces.

Explore hand scale ↗
A STARTING PROTOCOL

Make a record.

Choose a deck, then a matrix with a stated row and column count or a five-card cross. The cross is dealt in this order: center, above, below, left, right. Each card is drawn without replacement. A new deck or layout starts a fresh session.

Keep the original observation, the method and any interpretation together in the record.

TRY THE EXPERIMENT / CARDS

Make a draw. Keep a record.

Spanish cards, American playing cards or Tarot de Marseille. Arrange a matrix or a five-card cross.

Matrix: one card per cell, in row order. Cross: 1 center, 2 above, 3 below, 4 left, 5 right. Changing a deck or layout begins a fresh deck and clears its record. Wide matrices scroll horizontally.

No jokers. Marseille includes 22 major and 56 minor arcana, with Justice VIII and Strength XI. Every deck uses original Kamala artwork. Open a card image for a larger view. Browse all three illustrated decks ↗

How this draw works

The server takes up to 128 KiB of JPEG image data from one fixed stream, with a two-second timeout, and mixes it with fresh system randomness using SHA-512. The browser uses the same source module as the standalone key tool and mixes this response with its own random seed and uses fresh browser random words for each result. Rejection sampling avoids modulo bias. If the sampler is unavailable, results use browser randomness and the status says so.

Samples are experimental: no physical entropy rate has been established. Camera delays and repeated frames are possible. No predictive meaning is assigned to results. History stays in this page and clears when you leave or reset.
